svg.title: The orbit race: planets with true relative periods
svg.desc: Animated top view of the eight planets orbiting the Sun counter-clockwise. Orbital periods are true relative to each other (1 Earth year = 4 s of animation; each planet's rotation lasts T × 4 s), so Mercury laps Earth about four times per year while Neptune barely moves. Distances are compressed: drawn radius ∝ √a, so Neptune's orbit (30.1 AU) is 5.5× Earth's instead of 30×. Planets start at their J2000 mean longitudes (252.25°, 181.98°, 100.46°, 355.45°, 34.40°, 49.94°, 313.23°, 304.88°; JPL 'Approximate Positions of the Planets'); orbits drawn circular. A three-digit counter ticks Earth years. Data (NASA NSSDCA fact sheets): Mercury a = 0.3871 AU, T = 0.2408467 y; Venus a = 0.72333 AU, T = 0.6151973 y; Earth a = 1.0 AU, T = 1.0000174 y; Mars a = 1.52368 AU, T = 1.8808476 y; Jupiter a = 5.2026 AU, T = 11.862615 y; Saturn a = 9.55491 AU, T = 29.447498 y; Uranus a = 19.21845 AU, T = 84.016846 y; Neptune a = 30.11039 AU, T = 164.79132 y.
svg.text: THE SOLAR SYSTEM · TRUE RELATIVE PERIODS
